affected_cohort: Express Entry candidates with at least 12 months of eligible Canadian work experience in qualifying high-wage occupations or a qualifying high-wage job offer; route-specific eligibility applies
mechanism: Work-experience CRS additions: 70 points at at least 2x median wage; 40 at at least 1.5x; 20 at at least 1.3x. Qualifying job-offer additions: 100, 70 and 50 points at the same wage thresholds. From 3 November, LMIA is not required for qualifying job-offer points and specified Federal Skilled Worker/Federal Skilled Trades eligibility. The work-experience and job-offer point routes are not combined; the higher applicable option is used.
model_treatment: Cohort-specific pathway/selection feature; encode separately from destination macro energy; no country-level ranking adjustment
counterfactual_design: Candidate-level event study or DiD comparing eligible high-wage occupations with closely matched near-threshold occupations before and after 3 November 2026; test pre-trends, occupation-specific shocks, threshold manipulation, profile composition and concurrent selection changes.
revision_note: Version 2 updates the prior 2026-11-07 evidence-log record from announced/not-yet-effective to effective; the earlier record is preserved.
evidence_note: IRCC backgrounder dated 16 October 2026; high-wage occupations are defined using occupation median wages relative to the overall Canadian workforce. Additional CRS points do not guarantee an invitation or permanent residence.

affected_cohort: Eligible newcomers and families with employer/community recommendations in participating rural communities; 14 communities currently participate
mechanism: The Rural Community Immigration Pilot is made permanent. The 2027-2029 Immigration Levels Plan targets 5,500 admission spaces for the permanent program; future expansion to additional communities is planned but not yet specified.
model_treatment: Cohort- and place-specific permanent-residence pathway linked to rural labour shortages and local employer/community partnerships; do not generalise to all Canadian destinations or all occupations
counterfactual_design: Matched-community DiD/event study comparing the 14 participating communities with comparable non-participating rural areas; selection into the pilot, local labour demand, housing and population trends require pre-trend/placebo/sensitivity checks.
revision_note: New event discovered in official IRCC release dated 9 November 2026.
evidence_note: The announcement states the program is permanent, continues the 14 current communities and assigns 5,500 admission spaces in the 2027-2029 plan; this is not evidence of realized admissions or causal retention effects.

affected_cohort: Adults and accompanied children whose asylum claim or further submissions are lodged on or after 2 March 2026 and who are granted refugee status or humanitarian protection; unaccompanied asylum-seeking children are an exception
mechanism: Initial permission to stay on a protection route is normally 30 months for qualifying post-2 March 2026 claims and is reviewed at renewal; protection is renewed where the need continues and safe return may be expected where the country is considered safe. Unaccompanied asylum-seeking children receive 5 years. Claims made on or before 1 March 2026 retain the prior 5-year minimum; dependants generally align with the principal claimant.
model_treatment: Asylum/refugee-cohort settlement-duration and return-risk feature; keep separate from skilled-worker pathways and general destination macro scores
counterfactual_design: Potential cohort event study comparing claim cohorts immediately before/after 2 March 2026, with origin-country conditions and claimant composition controls; concurrent asylum reforms, selection and safe-return decisions make identification difficult; test pre-trends and placebo dates.
revision_note: Newly documented in the current event register; announcement/effective date precedes this run and is recorded as a backfill, not a new 15 November policy change.
evidence_note: Home Office announcement and Immigration Rules Part 11 confirm the 30-month rule from 2 March 2026, with the 5-year unaccompanied-child exception and pre-change transitional treatment.
